problem: Existence of perfect cuboids and associated cuboid conjectures
missing_details: Definition of Euler brick and its Diophantine equations for face diagonals
Identification of variables: edges a,b,c; face diagonals d,e,f; space diagonal g
Domain specification: all variables are positive integers
Additional Diophantine equation for space diagonal: a^2+b^2+c^2=g^2
Precise statement of the open existence question for perfect cuboids
Explicit form and parameter conditions for the three univariate polynomials in the cuboid conjectures
Irreducibility requirement over the ring of integers ℤ for each polynomial
refined_question: Does there exist a perfect cuboid, namely positive integers a,b,c,d,e,f,g satisfying simultaneously the four Diophantine equations a^2 + b^2 = d^2, a^2 + c^2 = e^2, b^2 + c^2 = f^2 (so that the rectangular cuboid with edges a,b,c has integer face diagonals d,e,f) and a^2 + b^2 + c^2 = g^2 (so that its space diagonal g is also integer)? Furthermore, for all choices of the integer parameters below, are the following univariate polynomials irreducible over ℤ? 1. For any two positive coprime integers a≠u, the degree-8 polynomial P_{au}(t)=t^8+6(u^2−a^2)t^6+(a^4−4a^2u^2+u^4)t^4−6a^2u^2(u^2−a^2)t^2+a^4u^4 is irreducible. 2. For any two positive coprime integers p≠q, the degree-10 polynomial Q_{pq}(t)=t^10+(2q^2+p^2)(3q^2−2p^2)t^8+(q^8+10p^2q^6+4p^4q^4−14p^6q^2+p^8)t^6−p^2q^2(q^8−14p^2q^6+4p^4q^4+10p^6q^2+p^8)t^4−p^6q^6(q^2+2p^2)(−2q^2+3p^2)t^2−p^10q^10 is irreducible. 3. For any three positive coprime integers a,b,u not satisfying any of the relations a=b, a=b=u, b·u=a^2, a·u=b^2, a=u, or b=u, the degree-12 polynomial P_{abu}(t)=t^12+(6u^2−2a^2−2b^2)t^10+(u^4+b^4+a^4+4a^2u^2+4b^2u^2−12a^2b^2)t^8+(6a^4u^2+6u^2b^4−8a^2b^2u^2−2u^4a^2−2u^4b^2−2a^4b^2−2b^4a^2)t^6+(4u^2b^4a^2+4a^4u^2b^2−12u^4a^2b^2+u^4a^4+u^4b^4+a^4b^4)t^4+(6a^4u^2b^4−2u^4a^4b^2−2u^4a^2b^4)t^2+u^4a^4b^4 is irreducible.
equivalent_formulation: The existence of a perfect cuboid is equivalent to the existence of a Heronian trirectangular tetrahedron with three mutually orthogonal integer edges a,b,c; passing between them by mapping the tetrahedron edges (a,b,c) to the cuboid edges (ab,ac,bc).
justification: The name “Existence of perfect cuboids and associated cuboid conjectures” omits critical details: it does not specify the underlying Diophantine system for edges and face diagonals, the additional space‐diagonal condition, the variables’ domains, nor the explicit form and irreducibility conditions of the three cuboid conjecture polynomials. The refined question provides all definitions, equations, parameter constraints, and the irreducibility requirements, making it fully self‐contained and faithful to the canonical sources.
